docs.text: Scope, architecture, and validation ¶ Package structure ¶ The distribution is named pystac-ext-application , while the import path is pystac.extensions.application . The wheel excludes the shared pystac.extensions initializer owned by PySTAC. ApplicationExtension.ext() returns a wrapper bound to an Item, Catalog, Collection, Asset, ItemAssetDefinition, or Link. The wrapper writes directly into the object's metadata dictionary, so serialization uses PySTAC's normal to_dict() method. The package stores application metadata; it does not run containers or workflows. Asset, item asset definition, and Link registration is managed through the owner. Item-owned Assets inherit missing Application fields from Item properties; explicit null masks inherited values. Collection-owned Assets do not inherit Collection fields. Nested template values ¶ Catalogs and Collections expose assetTemplates as a map and linkTemplates as a list. Both contain AssetTemplate wrappers. Setters encode wrappers into plain JSON containers. Getters wrap the stored nested dictionaries by reference, so editing a retrieved template changes the owning STAC object's serialized metadata. AssetTemplate.from_dict() also wraps by reference unless copy=True is requested. Unknown JSON members survive wrapping. The module is generated: changes to schema-defined fields belong in the source schema and generation workflow. Collection summaries ¶ Collections support both direct metadata through ext() and summaries through summaries() . The summary helper exposes container, entrypoint, and languages. It preserves complete lists, ranges, and JSON Schema dictionaries and replaces the previous representation when a summary is assigned. It does not compute summaries from Items. Validation boundaries ¶ Type annotations describe expected values but do not enforce every constraint at runtime. Field access checks target applicability, and template decoding checks the shapes of maps, lists, and nested objects. Reading or writing metadata does not perform full JSON Schema validation. apply() checks all supplied field names and their applicability before changing metadata. Omitted fields are preserved; None removes a field. This preflight check does not validate all supplied values or guarantee rollback for arbitrary setter failures. set_null() stores explicit JSON null without checking whether the schema permits it. For full STAC and extension validation, install PySTAC's validation extra with python -m pip install "pystac[validation]" and call item.validate() or validate the owning STAC object. Validation may retrieve remote schemas, so the referenced schema URLs must be accessible or supplied through an application-configured validator. Neither apply() nor to_dict() performs JSON Schema validation. The field reference describes supported properties and summaries. Schema registration and versions ¶ SCHEMA_URI identifies Application v0.1.0. has_extension() checks for this exact URI. ext() requires registration unless add_if_missing=True is supplied; for owned objects, registration is checked or added on the owner. Adding the current URI does not migrate older metadata. The module does not expose migration hooks.

docs.text: Install and build ¶ Install the library ¶ The package declares Python 3.10 or later and PySTAC >=1,<2 . The test matrix covers Python 3.10–3.14. python -m pip install pystac-ext-application python -c "from pystac.extensions.application import ApplicationExtension; print(ApplicationExtension.get_schema_uri())" Install from a checkout ¶ git clone https://github.com/Terradue/pystac-ext-application.git cd pystac-ext-application python -m pip install -e . If an existing editable installation predates a packaging change, repeat the editable install in that environment. Preview the documentation ¶ Install the documentation tools in your development environment: python -m pip install "mkdocs<2" mkdocs-material "mkdocstrings[python]" "pymdown-extensions<12" mkdocs serve The PyMdown upper bound keeps the highlighting API compatible with mkdocstrings 1.0.x. Build with warnings treated as errors: mkdocs build --strict Run repository checks ¶ With Hatch installed, run these commands from the checkout: hatch run dev:check hatch run dev:typecheck hatch run dev:security hatch run test:test

docs.text: Work with Application metadata ¶ Run the tutorial first. The examples below continue from its item , application , imports, and timestamp utilities, and can be executed in order. Update, remove, or explicitly null a field ¶ application = ApplicationExtension . ext ( item ) application . apply ( container = "podman" , entrypoint = None ) assert application . languages == [ "CWL" ] assert "application:entrypoint" not in item . properties application . set_null ( "entrypoint" ) assert item . properties [ "application:entrypoint" ] is None application . clear ( "entrypoint" ) assert "application:entrypoint" not in item . properties apply() preserves omitted fields. Assigning None removes a field; set_null() stores explicit JSON null, whose validity depends on the schema. clear() removes a field using its Python attribute name and is safe to repeat. Unknown or inapplicable names passed to apply() are rejected before any fields change. Attach asset fields ¶ asset = pystac . Asset ( href = "https://example.org/main.cwl" ) item . add_asset ( "workflow" , asset ) asset_application = ApplicationExtension . ext ( asset ) assert asset_application . container == "podman" asset_application . container = "docker" assert asset . extra_fields [ "application:container" ] == "docker" assert application . container == "podman" asset_application . container = None assert asset_application . container == "podman" asset_application . set_null ( "container" ) assert asset_application . container is None asset_application . clear ( "container" ) assert asset_application . container == "podman" Asset fields are written to asset.extra_fields . When an Asset belongs to an Item, absent fields fall back to the Item's properties. Explicit null on the Asset masks the inherited value; clearing the field restores inheritance. Collection-owned Assets do not inherit Collection fields. Attach Assets, Links, and item asset definitions to their owner before registering the extension. add_if_missing=True registers the schema on that owner. Set Collection metadata and summaries ¶ collection = pystac . Collection ( id = "example-applications" , description = "Application examples" , extent = pystac . Extent ( pystac . SpatialExtent ([ - 180.0 , - 90.0 , 180.0 , 90.0 ]), pystac . TemporalExtent ([ None , None ]), ), license = "proprietary" , ) collection_application = ApplicationExtension . ext ( collection , add_if_missing = True ) collection_application . container = "docker" summaries = ApplicationExtension . summaries ( collection ) summaries . container = [ "docker" , "podman" ] summaries . languages = [ "CWL" , "Python" ] assert summaries . container == [ "docker" , "podman" ] assert collection . summaries . to_dict ()[ "application:languages" ] == [ "CWL" , "Python" ] summaries . languages = None assert "application:languages" not in collection . summaries . to_dict () ext(collection) accesses Collection metadata; summaries(collection) accesses its summaries. Summary setters replace the entire summary for the selected field. Getters preserve full lists, ranges, or JSON Schema objects. The helper exposes container , entrypoint , and languages ; it does not aggregate Items or provide an apply() method. Define asset and link templates ¶ from pystac.extensions.application import AssetTemplate template = AssetTemplate . create ( container = "docker" , entrypoint = "main.cwl" , languages = [ "CWL" ], ) collection_application . assetTemplates = { "workflow" : template } collection_application . linkTemplates = [ template ] asset_templates = collection_application . assetTemplates assert asset_templates is not None asset_templates [ "workflow" ] . entrypoint = "updated.cwl" assert collection . extra_fields [ "assetTemplates" ][ "workflow" ][ "application:entrypoint" ] == "updated.cwl" assert template . entrypoint == "main.cwl" assetTemplates and linkTemplates are available only on Catalogs and Collections. Both use AssetTemplate values. Setters encode these values into plain JSON dictionaries; getters return wrappers backed by the stored dictionaries, so nested edits are live. AssetTemplate.create() omits unspecified members. apply() preserves omitted members and removes those set to None . from_dict() preserves unknown members and shares the supplied dictionary by default; use copy=True for an independent deep copy. to_dict() returns the live backing dictionary. Use Collection item asset definitions ¶ collection . item_assets = { "workflow" : pystac . ItemAssetDefinition ({ "roles" : [ "data" ]}), } definition = collection . item_assets [ "workflow" ] definition_application = ApplicationExtension . ext ( definition ) definition_application . entrypoint = "main.cwl" assert definition . properties [ "application:entrypoint" ] == "main.cwl" Retrieve definitions through collection.item_assets so they have an owner. Fields are written to the definition's properties dictionary, and extension registration is checked on its Collection. Attach Link metadata and use Catalogs ¶ catalog = pystac . Catalog ( id = "applications" , description = "Application catalog" ) catalog_application = ApplicationExtension . ext ( catalog , add_if_missing = True ) catalog_application . languages = [ "CWL" ] link = pystac . Link ( rel = "related" , target = "https://example.org/application.json" ) catalog . add_link ( link ) link_application = ApplicationExtension . ext ( link ) link_application . entrypoint = "main.cwl" assert link . extra_fields [ "application:entrypoint" ] == "main.cwl" Catalog metadata uses catalog.extra_fields . Link metadata uses link.extra_fields , with registration checked on the Link's owner.

STAC field Python property Value type Supported targets application:container container str All supported targets application:entrypoint entrypoint str All supported targets application:languages languages list[str] All supported targets assetTemplates assetTemplates dict[str, AssetTemplate] Catalogs and Collections linkTemplates linkTemplates list[AssetTemplate] Catalogs and Collections The template field names have no application: prefix. Their Python properties retain the schema's camelCase spelling. AssetTemplate exposes the same container , entrypoint , and languages members as the extension, with prefixed keys in its backing dictionary. Storage and inheritance ¶ Items and item asset definitions store fields in properties . Catalogs, Collections, Assets, and Links use extra_fields . Wrappers update these dictionaries directly. Item-owned Assets fall back to Item properties for missing fields. An explicit Asset null overrides that fallback. Other targets do not inherit metadata from their owners. Update semantics ¶ Getters return None for absent fields without an inherited value, or for explicit null. Property setters and apply() remove fields assigned None . apply() preserves omitted fields, including when called without arguments. set_null(name) stores explicit JSON null; schema validation determines whether it is allowed. clear(name) removes a field and does nothing if it is already absent. clear() and set_null() accept Python attribute names and raise KeyError for unknown names. apply() raises TypeError for unknown names and pystac.ExtensionTypeError for fields unsupported on the target, before applying any updates. Accessing or setting template fields on targets other than Catalogs and Collections raises pystac.ExtensionTypeError . Nested templates ¶ AssetTemplate.create() accepts optional typed members and omits unspecified values. AssetTemplate.apply() preserves unspecified values and removes members set to None . clear() and set_null() distinguish absence from explicit null. AssetTemplate.from_dict(properties) wraps the dictionary by reference and retains unknown keys. copy=True makes a deep copy. to_dict() returns the live dictionary. Extension template getters return live nested wrappers; setters encode supplied wrappers into plain JSON containers. Malformed stored template maps or arrays raise TypeError when read. Each nested template must be backed by a dictionary. These structural checks are not full schema validation. Collection summaries ¶ ApplicationExtension.summaries(collection) exposes container , entrypoint , and languages , mapped to their corresponding application: keys. Each property accepts a list, a pystac.RangeSummary , a JSON Schema dictionary, or None . Getters return the complete stored summary, converting dictionaries with both minimum and maximum to a RangeSummary . Missing summaries return None . Setters replace the previous summary representation; assigning None removes it. Whether a summary value is valid for a field is determined by the schema. The helper does not compute summaries from Items and has no apply() method.

docs.text: Tutorials ¶ Create your first Application Item , attach container, entrypoint, and language metadata, and serialize it to STAC JSON. The example runs without a catalog service.

docs.text: Create your first Application Item , attach container, entrypoint, and language metadata, and serialize it to STAC JSON. The example runs without a catalog service.
docs.title: Tutorials

docs.text: Create an Application Item ¶ Install the package before running this complete example. It creates an Item carrying application metadata and reads that metadata back after serialization. from datetime import datetime , timezone import pystac from pystac.extensions.application import ApplicationExtension item = pystac . Item ( id = "example-application" , geometry = None , bbox = None , datetime = datetime ( 2026 , 1 , 1 , tzinfo = timezone . utc ), properties = { "title" : "Application example" }, ) application = ApplicationExtension . ext ( item , add_if_missing = True ) application . apply ( container = "docker" , entrypoint = "main.cwl" , languages = [ "CWL" ], ) serialized = item . to_dict () assert ApplicationExtension . get_schema_uri () in serialized [ "stac_extensions" ] assert serialized [ "properties" ][ "application:container" ] == "docker" assert serialized [ "properties" ][ "application:entrypoint" ] == "main.cwl" assert serialized [ "properties" ][ "application:languages" ] == [ "CWL" ] restored_item = pystac . Item . from_dict ( serialized ) restored = ApplicationExtension . ext ( restored_item ) assert restored . container == application . container assert restored . entrypoint == application . entrypoint assert restored . languages == application . languages add_if_missing=True registers the extension schema on the Item. Subsequent calls to ApplicationExtension.ext(item) require that registration. The wrapper stores metadata; it does not execute the application. The core Item datetime is supplied by the caller and is independent of the Application fields. to_dict() serializes the Item without running JSON Schema validation. See validation boundaries for the distinction.
